system.name: GenAuction
system.one_liner: Generative ad auction in which a Transformer-based Generator proposes candidate page views, an Evaluator picks the best, and a VCG module sets payments.

content.variant_note: wide left-to-right block diagram of a generator (two repeated PV-Generator modules), an evaluator and a payment module, with input, output and payment rows under the frame
content.argues: Selecting whole page views with a generator and an evaluator, instead of ranking ads one by one, allocates ads end to end and prices them with VCG.
content.subject: Repeated PV-Generator modules, an Evaluator with a CTR model and a VCG Payment module, with input, output and payment rows below.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each kind of data one dashed-outline colour and keep it on the tile columns, the arrows and the rows beneath the frame, so a long left-to-right mechanism can be followed by colour alone; show a repeated module twice with an ellipsis instead of drawing it N times.
lessons.suits: auction, ranking or generator-evaluator pipelines with several kinds of intermediate sets and system-level inputs, outputs and payments.

evidence: GenAuction consists of three primary components: the Generator, which is to create a set of candidate PVs
the Evaluator, which assesses the candidate PVs to select a winning PV
we use embedding layers to extract the embeddings from raw sparse features

summary: GenAuction is a generative ad auction that selects winning page views (PVs) instead of single ads. The figure is a wide left-to-right block diagram inside a titled frame. The Generator holds two repeated PV-Generator modules; each has a Selector (Embedding, Transformer, Masking) that outputs candidate ads and a Concator (Concat, Beam Search) that assembles candidate PVs, and a PV Embedding passes the first PV on to the second generator. The candidate PVs, Output (PVX), go to the Evaluator, a stack of PV Embedding, a contextual-aware CTR model, PV Embedding, Transformer and an MLP with soft-max and argmax, which yields the chosen PV. A VCG Payment module turns it into payments. Dashed outlines in red, green, purple, blue and yellow follow each kind of data to the Input, Output and Payment rows beneath.
